briefing.headline: 9 high-priority items in the latest EM scan
briefing.summary: Top sources today: AJEM, Annals of Emergency Medicine, EMJ. Main themes: policy statements, consensus guidance, guideline or formal recommendation. Best early reads: Prospective validation of HACOR score for HFNO failure in emergency department patients with acute respiratory failure; Clinical Policy: A Critical Issue Related to Direct Oral Anticoagulants in Adult Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department.
briefing.editorialHeadline: Today in EM: respiratory support, haemorrhage, and time-critical resuscitation
briefing.editorialSummary: Today’s strongest practice-facing reads span three recurring ED decisions: recognising failure early, choosing haemostatic therapy, and acting before physiology deteriorates. The lead study supports reassessing HACOR at 60 minutes during HFNO; new ACEP policy reviews reversal for major DOAC bleeding; and practical guidance covers resuscitative thoracotomy, crush injury, procedural sedation, regional analgesia, early norepinephrine, and high-risk airway management. Most findings should inform protocols and bedside judgement rather than trigger isolated practice changes.

dailyEditorial.title: Prospective validation of HACOR score for HFNO failure in emergency department patients with acute respiratory failure
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Recalculate HACOR after the first hour of HFNO and escalate concern when it remains high; do not adopt the exploratory ≥8 threshold without further validation.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: Prospective ED validation found the HACOR score at 60 minutes discriminated HFNO failure substantially better than the admission score, without detected miscalibration.
dailyEditorial.summary: Prospective ED validation found the HACOR score at 60 minutes discriminated HFNO failure substantially better than the admission score, without detected miscalibration. The established >5 threshold remained useful, while a proposed ≥8 threshold is exploratory.

dailyEditorial.title: Clinical Policy: A Critical Issue Related to Direct Oral Anticoagulants in Adult Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Use this policy to review your ED pathway for life-threatening DOAC bleeding, including drug-specific reversal, PCC access, consultation, and time-to-treatment.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: ACEP’s new clinical policy evaluates whether agent-specific antidotes improve outcomes versus usual care, including prothrombin complex concentrate, for adults with major symptomatic bleeding while taking a direct oral…
dailyEditorial.summary: ACEP’s new clinical policy evaluates whether agent-specific antidotes improve outcomes versus usual care, including prothrombin complex concentrate, for adults with major symptomatic bleeding while taking a direct oral anticoagulant.

dailyEditorial.title: Emergency thoracotomy: how to do it in 2026
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Useful for trauma governance and rehearsal: align local indications, equipment, roles, and stop criteria before the next rare time-critical case.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: A contemporary practical guide updates indications, survival windows, procedural steps, troubleshooting, team factors, and safety considerations for emergency thoracotomy.
dailyEditorial.summary: A contemporary practical guide updates indications, survival windows, procedural steps, troubleshooting, team factors, and safety considerations for emergency thoracotomy.

dailyEditorial.title: Unscheduled Procedural Sedation Multidisciplinary Delphi Consensus Guidelines, Part 1: Principles, Oversight, and Quality Monitoring
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Use the full document as a governance audit: credentialing, adverse-event review, data collection, escalation standards, and multidisciplinary ownership are the likely high-value domains.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: Part 1 of the multidisciplinary Delphi consensus addresses principles, oversight, and quality monitoring for unscheduled procedural sedation.
dailyEditorial.summary: Part 1 of the multidisciplinary Delphi consensus addresses principles, oversight, and quality monitoring for unscheduled procedural sedation. The available excerpt is publication boilerplate, not the recommendations themselves.

dailyEditorial.title: Whole Blood Versus Component Therapy for Out-of-Hospital Trauma Resuscitation
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Read the full review before changing blood strategy; focus locally on indication, product availability, cold chain, transfusion governance, and transition to hospital massive transfusion.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: This evidence review discusses prehospital type O whole blood versus component therapy for traumatic haemorrhage, anchored to the cited Sperry trial.
dailyEditorial.summary: This evidence review discusses prehospital type O whole blood versus component therapy for traumatic haemorrhage, anchored to the cited Sperry trial. The feed excerpt does not provide enough results for a firm efficacy conclusion.

dailyEditorial.title: Ultrasound-guided pericapsular nerve group block versus intravenous morphine for pain management in older adults with hip fractures: a randomised controlled trial in the emergency department
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Consider PENG block as an opioid-sparing option for hip-fracture pain where trained clinicians, ultrasound, consent, and local anaesthetic safety systems are available.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: In an ED randomised trial of older adults with hip fracture, ultrasound-guided PENG block produced better early pain relief than intravenous morphine, with rescue analgesia and adverse events assessed as secondary outco…
dailyEditorial.summary: In an ED randomised trial of older adults with hip fracture, ultrasound-guided PENG block produced better early pain relief than intravenous morphine, with rescue analgesia and adverse events assessed as secondary outcomes.

dailyEditorial.title: Journal update monthly top five
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Treat this as a rapid evidence scan; for medium-vessel occlusion decisions, check the trial’s patient selection, effect estimates, harms, and fit with local stroke pathways.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: EMJ’s monthly evidence roundup leads with ORIENTAL-MeVO, an open-label, blinded-outcome multicentre RCT of thrombectomy for medium-vessel occlusion stroke, alongside four other selected studies.
dailyEditorial.summary: EMJ’s monthly evidence roundup leads with ORIENTAL-MeVO, an open-label, blinded-outcome multicentre RCT of thrombectomy for medium-vessel occlusion stroke, alongside four other selected studies.

dailyEditorial.title: Early management of crush injury and crush syndrome: a Faculty of Pre-Hospital Care consensus statement
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Read early if your service manages entrapment incidents; reconcile fluid, electrolyte, analgesia, extrication, monitoring, and destination recommendations with local major-incident protocols.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: A Faculty of Pre-Hospital Care consensus statement offers structured, practical UK guidance for early crush injury and crush syndrome management after evidence review and expert consensus.
dailyEditorial.summary: A Faculty of Pre-Hospital Care consensus statement offers structured, practical UK guidance for early crush injury and crush syndrome management after evidence review and expert consensus.

dailyEditorial.title: Is intranasal adrenaline effective for the treatment of anaphylaxis?
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Intramuscular epinephrine remains the emergency standard unless authoritative guidance changes; assess the full review before considering intranasal products in any pathway.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: A short-cut review identified eight directly relevant papers comparing intranasal with intramuscular epinephrine for rapid symptom control in anaphylaxis.
dailyEditorial.summary: A short-cut review identified eight directly relevant papers comparing intranasal with intramuscular epinephrine for rapid symptom control in anaphylaxis. The feed excerpt does not establish equivalence or superiority.

dailyEditorial.title: Potential Risks With the SPEAR®, a New Device Marketed for Out-of-Hospital Needle Decompression of the Chest
dailyEditorial.takeaway: EMS medical directors should urgently review the full letter, device instructions, insertion-site policy, training, and adverse-event reporting before deployment.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: A safety letter warns of potential complications from the 9.5 cm, 10-gauge SPEAR catheter marketed for blind prehospital needle decompression and questions aspects of its insertion instructions.
dailyEditorial.summary: A safety letter warns of potential complications from the 9.5 cm, 10-gauge SPEAR catheter marketed for blind prehospital needle decompression and questions aspects of its insertion instructions.

dailyEditorial.title: Sickle Cell Acute Pain Episodes: Lessons Learned from the Prematurely Halted PECARN STArT Trial
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Do not add arginine on these data; use the trial to examine delays and variation in your own sickle-cell analgesia pathway. PECARN’s phase 3 STArT trial of intravenous arginine for paediatric sickle-cell acute pain was stopped early for futility.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: PECARN’s phase 3 STArT trial of intravenous arginine for paediatric sickle-cell acute pain was stopped early for futility.
dailyEditorial.summary: PECARN’s phase 3 STArT trial of intravenous arginine for paediatric sickle-cell acute pain was stopped early for futility. The commentary highlights striking between-hospital variation in time to crisis resolution and challenges in defining the enrolled syndrome.

dailyEditorial.title: Association between the time to norepinephrine initiation and mortality in patients with sepsis
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Avoid prolonged hypotension while repeatedly giving fluid: establish a pathway for timely norepinephrine when shock persists, but do not interpret the 60-minute association as a definitive causal threshold.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: In an observational sepsis cohort, longer time to norepinephrine was associated with higher 28-day mortality; initiation within 60 minutes of hypotension was associated with lower risk.
dailyEditorial.summary: In an observational sepsis cohort, longer time to norepinephrine was associated with higher 28-day mortality; initiation within 60 minutes of hypotension was associated with lower risk. Residual confounding limits causal inference.

dailyEditorial.title: JC: Manual pressure augmentation during cardiac arrest: another lesson in physiology versus outcome
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Do not equate improved impedance with clinical benefit; examine outcome data and operational risks before adding manual pressure augmentation to arrest protocols.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: A review of the AUGMENT-VA randomised trial asks whether manual pressure augmentation during defibrillation converts a favourable physiological effect—lower transthoracic impedance—into better patient outcomes.
dailyEditorial.summary: A review of the AUGMENT-VA randomised trial asks whether manual pressure augmentation during defibrillation converts a favourable physiological effect—lower transthoracic impedance—into better patient outcomes.

dailyEditorial.title: EMCrit 432 – Members’ Airway Cases and Q&A
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Use the cases for team rehearsal: optimise physiology before induction, anticipate peri-intubation arrest, and build explicit rescue plans for anatomically and metabolically difficult airways.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: A case-based airway discussion covers severe obstruction, high-risk hypoxaemia, CHOP assessment, induction in cardiogenic shock, and extreme metabolic acidosis.
dailyEditorial.summary: A case-based airway discussion covers severe obstruction, high-risk hypoxaemia, CHOP assessment, induction in cardiogenic shock, and extreme metabolic acidosis. It is expert education rather than comparative evidence.

dailyEditorial.title: Primary survey: highlights from this issue
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Use this as a navigation piece; read the original PENG trial rather than relying on the editor’s summary for practice decisions. The issue overview highlights a randomised comparison of PENG block with intravenous morphine for hip fracture and points readers to other clinically relevant work in the same EMJ issue.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: The issue overview highlights a randomised comparison of PENG block with intravenous morphine for hip fracture and points readers to other clinically relevant work in the same EMJ issue.
dailyEditorial.summary: The issue overview highlights a randomised comparison of PENG block with intravenous morphine for hip fracture and points readers to other clinically relevant work in the same EMJ issue.

dailyEditorial.title: Common femoral artery access in emergency medicine
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Services developing ECPR or endovascular resuscitation should deliberately train ultrasound-guided CFA access and standardise equipment, confirmation, complication management, and credentialing.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: A practical review argues that common femoral artery access is increasingly relevant for central pressure monitoring and endovascular resuscitation, and outlines Seldinger-guided sheath insertion and training needs.
dailyEditorial.summary: A practical review argues that common femoral artery access is increasingly relevant for central pressure monitoring and endovascular resuscitation, and outlines Seldinger-guided sheath insertion and training needs.

dailyEditorial.title: Response From Authors to the Letter to the Editor
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Audit undertriage among critically ill patients and link triage accuracy to time-critical processes; the association does not by itself prove that undertriage caused worse outcomes.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: In response to correspondence, the authors reiterate findings from more than 5.3 million encounters: over one-third of the sickest patients were undertriaged, and undertriage was associated with a median eight-minute de…
dailyEditorial.summary: In response to correspondence, the authors reiterate findings from more than 5.3 million encounters: over one-third of the sickest patients were undertriaged, and undertriage was associated with a median eight-minute delay versus correct high-acuity triage.

dailyEditorial.title: Clinical Trial Probes Fluid Choice in Suspected Pediatric Septic Shock
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Either crystalloid appears reasonable from this report; review the trial’s endpoints and confidence intervals before claiming equivalence or revising paediatric sepsis protocols.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: A report on PECARN’s PRoMPT BOLUS trial says normal saline and balanced crystalloids were both safe and effective in suspected paediatric septic shock.
dailyEditorial.summary: A report on PECARN’s PRoMPT BOLUS trial says normal saline and balanced crystalloids were both safe and effective in suspected paediatric septic shock. Detailed outcomes are not present in the feed excerpt.

dailyEditorial.title: Abstracts from international Emergency Medicine journals
dailyEditorial.takeaway: Use the collection to identify papers relevant to local priorities, then appraise the original studies before translating findings into practice.
dailyEditorial.shortSummary: EMJ curates abstracts selected by partner emergency-medicine journals, including a randomised trial of intranasal versus subcutaneous ketamine for acute traumatic pain.
dailyEditorial.summary: EMJ curates abstracts selected by partner emergency-medicine journals, including a randomised trial of intranasal versus subcutaneous ketamine for acute traumatic pain. It is a discovery collection, not a single synthesis.
